source_evidence.anchor: standing rectangular full-rank setup and Algorithm 2 (CGS-P)
source_evidence.observation: The standing setup is A in R^(m x n), m >= n, rank(A) = n, with columns a_1,...,a_n. Exact arithmetic gives A = QR, Q^T Q = I_n, and an upper-triangular nonsingular R. The text distinguishes standard CGS-S from the Cholesky-like CGS-P diagonal computation.

Algorithm 2 computes s_k = Q_(k-1)^T a_k, v_k = a_k - Q_(k-1)s_k, psi_k = ||a_k||_2, phi_k = ||s_k||_2, r_kk = sqrt(psi_k-phi_k)sqrt(psi_k+phi_k), and q_k = v_k/r_kk. The arithmetic is assumed to satisfy IEEE floating-point behavior, with fl(x+y) = (x+y)(1+delta), |delta| <= epsilon_M, for normalized-range results, and second-order terms are neglected through a stated linear approximation.

The theorem defines c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4, A_k, and kappa_2(R_k), assumes c_4(m,k) epsilon_M kappa_2(R_k)^2 < 1 for every prefix k, and states five simultaneous first-order conclusions: factorization residual, normal-equation residual, norm agreement, loss of orthogonality, and a bound on ||Q_k||_2.

source_evidence.anchor: unnumbered exact identity and following norm estimate deriving (7)
source_evidence.observation: The proof writes Q_k = (A_k + Delta A_k)R_k^(-1) and exactly decomposes I-Q_k^TQ_k as R_k^(-T)(E_k-A_k^T Delta A_k-(Delta A_k)^T A_k-(Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k)R_k^(-1). Applying (4)-(6) produces the c_4(m,k)kappa_2(R_k)^2 epsilon_M bound plus O(epsilon_M^2).
When the assumptions of Theorem 1 are not satisfied, the paper says it is possible that phi_k >= psi_k, causing Algorithm 2 to break down and produce Q and R that are not real matrices.

binders: Integers m and n and a real matrix A in R^(m x n), with m >= n and rank(A) = n; these are standing assumptions inherited from the setup preceding Algorithm 2. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: standing rectangular full-rank setup.)

For every k in {1,...,n}, A_k is the matrix formed from the first k columns of A, while Q_k in R^(m x k) and R_k in R^(k x k) are the corresponding computed prefixes produced by Algorithm 2; the dimensions follow from the stated block constructions and theorem equations. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 block construction; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1.)

epsilon_M is the machine unit, and c_i(m,k), kappa_2(R_k), Delta A_k, E_k, and mu_k have the definitions appearing in equations (2)-(7). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definitions (2) and Theorem 1.)
hypotheses: A is a full-column-rank real m-by-n matrix with m >= n. This is inherited rather than repeated in Theorem 1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: standing rectangular full-rank setup.)

Q and R, including every Q_k and R_k, are the floating-point outputs of Algorithm 2, CGS-P. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: opening sentence of Theorem 1.)

For every k in {1,...,n}, c_4(m,k) epsilon_M kappa_2(R_k)^2 < 1. The hypothesis is imposed prefix by prefix before the conclusions are asserted prefix by prefix. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, inequality (3).)

Floating-point arithmetic satisfies the stated IEEE normalized-range relative-error model, and the analysis uses a first-order approximation that treats O(epsilon_M^2) as insignificant for a modest function p(n). (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point model and linear approximation.)
conclusions: For every k = 1,...,n, Q_k R_k - A_k = Delta A_k and ||Delta A_k||_2 <= c_1(m,k)||A_k||_2 epsilon_M, to within O(epsilon_M^2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equation (4).)
For every k = 1,...,n, R_k^T R_k - A_k^T A_k = E_k and ||E_k||_2 <= c_2(m,k)||A_k||_2^2 epsilon_M, to within O(epsilon_M^2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equation (5).)
For every k = 1,...,n, ||R_k||_2 = ||A_k||_2(1+mu_k), where |mu_k| <= c_3(m,k)epsilon_M, to within O(epsilon_M^2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equation (6).)

For every k = 1,...,n, ||I-Q_k^T Q_k||_2 <= c_4(m,k)kappa_2(R_k)^2 epsilon_M, to within O(epsilon_M^2). Dimensionally, the displayed I is I_k. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equation (7).)
For every k = 1,...,n, ||Q_k||_2 <= sqrt(2), to within the theorem's stated omission of O(epsilon_M^2) terms. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equation (8).)
definitions_and_conventions: A = (a_1,...,a_n), Q = (q_1,...,q_n), and R = (r_jk); Q_k and R_k are assembled column by column. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: notational conventions; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2.)
Algorithm 2 initializes r_11 = ||a_1||_2, q_1 = a_1/r_11, R_1 = (r_11), and Q_1 = (q_1). (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 initialization.)

For k >= 2, Algorithm 2 uses s_k = Q_(k-1)^T a_k, v_k = a_k-Q_(k-1)s_k, psi_k = ||a_k||_2, phi_k = ||s_k||_2, r_kk = sqrt(psi_k-phi_k)sqrt(psi_k+phi_k), and q_k = v_k/r_kk. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 loop.)
c_1(m,1) = 1, while c_1(m,k) = 2sqrt(2)mk + 2sqrt(k) for k = 2,...,n. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2), definition of c_1.)
c_2(m,1) = m+2, while c_2(m,k) = 3.5mk^2 - 1.5mk + 16k for k = 2,...,n. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2), definition of c_2.)
c_3(m,k) = 0.5c_2(m,k), and c_4(m,k) = c_2(m,k)+2c_1(m,k). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2), definitions of c_3 and c_4.)
kappa_2(R_k) = ||R_k||_2 ||R_k^(-1)||_2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition immediately before Theorem 1.)

Delta A_k and E_k are defined by the signed residual equalities Q_kR_k-A_k = Delta A_k and R_k^TR_k-A_k^TA_k = E_k; reversing either sign would change the proof identity. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equations (4) and (5); PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: exact identity deriving (7).)
implicit_context: The exact-arithmetic target is a QR factorization with Q^TQ = I_n and upper-triangular nonsingular R, but Theorem 1 concerns the computed floating-point Q_k and R_k. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: exact factorization setup; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: computed matrices in Theorem 1.)

The paper uses the same unhatted symbols for algorithm variables and computed outputs; computed status is conveyed in prose rather than typographically. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and floating-point setup; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: 'computed matrices R_k and Q_k'.)
Because Q_k has k columns, the identity matrix in ||I-Q_k^TQ_k||_2 is dimensionally I_k, although equation (7) prints only I. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (7) and definition of A_k.)

The restriction (3) is stated to assure that R is nonsingular and that conclusions (7) and (8) hold; the paper says weaker nonsingularity and bounded-Q assumptions would yield bounds similar to (4)-(6). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: paragraph immediately following Theorem 1.)
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is specifically linked to Algorithm 2, the Cholesky-like or pythagorean classical Gram-Schmidt algorithm CGS-P. Its defining diagonal update is r_kk = sqrt(psi_k-phi_k)sqrt(psi_k+phi_k), with psi_k = ||a_k||_2 and phi_k = ||s_k||_2. Standard CGS-S instead takes r_kk = ||v_k||_2, and the paper explicitly says the analogous stated lemma is not correct for Algorithm 1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: distinction from standard CGS; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and paragraph following Lemma 1.)
numerical_model: The arithmetic is assumed to satisfy the IEEE floating-point standard. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point-model paragraph.)

The explicitly displayed local model is fl(x+y) = (x+y)(1+delta), with |delta| <= epsilon_M, for results in the normalized range. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: displayed IEEE arithmetic equation.)

The paper uses (1+epsilon_M)^(p(n)) = 1+p(n)epsilon_M+O(epsilon_M^2) for a modest p(n) and assumes the O(epsilon_M^2) contribution is insignificant. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation.)

A_k is the original input prefix, whereas Q_k and R_k are computed matrices; Delta A_k and E_k measure their discrepancies from exact algebraic relations involving A_k. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equations (4) and (5).)
error_notions: Delta A_k is the forward factorization residual in Q_kR_k-A_k, bounded relative to ||A_k||_2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (4).)
E_k is the normal-equation or Cholesky-factor residual R_k^TR_k-A_k^TA_k, bounded relative to ||A_k||_2^2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (5).)
mu_k is a relative discrepancy between ||R_k||_2 and ||A_k||_2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (6).)
The selected quantity ||I-Q_k^TQ_k||_2 is loss of column orthogonality, not a factorization residual. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (7).)

The proof derives the orthogonality error from both E_k and Delta A_k through I-Q_k^TQ_k = R_k^(-T)(E_k-A_k^T Delta A_k-(Delta A_k)^T A_k-(Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k)R_k^(-1). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: unnumbered exact identity deriving (7).)
norms: Every final theorem bound uses the subscript-2 norm. For vectors this is the Euclidean norm; for matrices the surrounding condition-number and singular-value formulas indicate the spectral operator 2-norm, although the selected setup does not separately define it. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: vector norm in the algorithms; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: kappa_2 definition and equations (4)-(9).)
The orthogonality defect is measured globally by the matrix 2-norm ||I_k-Q_k^TQ_k||_2, not entrywise and not in Frobenius norm. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (7).)

The condition-number factor is squared: kappa_2(R_k)^2 = ||R_k||_2^2||R_k^(-1)||_2^2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition of kappa_2 and equation (7); PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: final norm estimate.)
constants_and_indexing: All hypotheses and conclusions are prefix-indexed for k = 1,...,n; c_1 and c_2 have distinct k=1 cases. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2) and Theorem 1.)
For k >= 2, c_1(m,k) = 2sqrt(2)mk+2sqrt(k), with m and k outside the square root except for the displayed sqrt(2) and sqrt(k). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2), c_1 branch.)
For k >= 2, c_2(m,k) = 3.5mk^2-1.5mk+16k; c_3 = c_2/2 and c_4 = c_2+2c_1. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2).)

The bound in (7) contains exactly one factor epsilon_M and the square of kappa_2(R_k); it is not stated with kappa_2(A_k), although the subsequent remark discusses a possible reformulation. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (7) and opening of Remark 1.)
higher_order_terms: Theorem 1 qualifies the complete list (4)-(8) by 'to within terms of O(epsilon_M^2)'; those terms are suppressed from the displayed theorem formulas. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: sentence immediately preceding equations (4)-(8).)

The proof of (7) explicitly retains +O(epsilon_M^2) while deriving c_4(m,k)kappa_2(R_k)^2 epsilon_M, confirming that the displayed theorem bound is a first-order statement rather than an unqualified exact inequality. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: following norm estimate deriving (7).)
The floating-point setup justifies this suppression by assuming O(epsilon_M^2) makes no significant contribution for modest p(n). (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation paragraph.)
exceptional_values: The displayed relative-error model is restricted to results in the normalized range; the cited passage gives no separate treatment of subnormal results, overflow, infinities, or NaNs. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: displayed IEEE arithmetic model and normalized-range qualification.)

Algorithm 2 requires real square roots of psi_k-phi_k and psi_k+phi_k and division by r_kk. Outside Theorem 1's assumptions, phi_k >= psi_k can cause breakdown and non-real Q and R. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 diagonal formula; PDF p. 7, printed p. 305, anchor: Remark 2.)

The paper states that restriction (3) assures nonsingularity of R; this supplies the invertibility needed by kappa_2(R_k), Q_k=(A_k+Delta A_k)R_k^(-1), and the orthogonality proof. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: paragraph after Theorem 1; PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: identity deriving (7).)

undebatable_constraints: The theorem applies to computed prefixes from Algorithm 2 (CGS-P), not standard Algorithm 1 (CGS-S). (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and paragraph following Lemma 1.)
The inherited input is a real full-column-rank A in R^(m x n) with m >= n. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: standing rectangular full-rank setup.)
Condition (3), c_4(m,k)epsilon_M kappa_2(R_k)^2 < 1, is required for every k before the theorem concludes the bounds for every k. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, inequality (3).)

The selected loss-of-orthogonality bound is ||I_k-Q_k^TQ_k||_2 <= c_4(m,k)kappa_2(R_k)^2 epsilon_M, subject to omitted O(epsilon_M^2) terms. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (7) and its first-order qualifier.)
c_4 is not an unspecified constant: c_4(m,k) = c_2(m,k)+2c_1(m,k), with c_1 and c_2 given piecewise in equation (2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: equation (2).)

The condition number in the theorem is that of computed R_k, namely ||R_k||_2||R_k^(-1)||_2, and it is squared in (3) and (7). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: kappa_2 definition and equations (3), (7).)

The enclosing theorem is multi-part and also asserts equations (4), (5), (6), and (8); extracting only (7) would omit explicit parts of Theorem 1. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equations (4)-(8).)

The proof of (7) necessarily uses both the normal-equation error E_k and the factorization error Delta A_k, including the quadratic term (Delta A_k)^T Delta A_k. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: exact identity and norm estimate deriving (7).)

The claims are first-order floating-point bounds with O(epsilon_M^2) omitted, not exact inequalities asserted uniformly without higher-order remainder. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: first-order qualifier; PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: proof remainder.)

ambiguities.issue: The theorem prints I rather than I_k in equation (7).
ambiguities.evidence: Q_k has k columns, so Q_k^TQ_k is k-by-k, while the displayed bound is ||I-Q_k^TQ_k||_2. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition of A_k and equation (7).)
ambiguities.impact: A formal rendering must choose I_k by dimensional inference, while recording that the subscript is absent from the printed equation.

ambiguities.issue: The matrix 2-norm is used but not separately defined in the selected setup.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper writes kappa_2(R_k)=||R_k||_2||R_k^(-1)||_2 and immediately relates these norms to singular-value/eigenvalue expressions. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: kappa_2 definition and equation (9).)
ambiguities.impact: The spectral operator norm is strongly indicated, but substituting the Frobenius norm or an entrywise norm would not be faithful.

ambiguities.issue: The hypothesis uses R_k^(-1) while the prose says the restriction assures nonsingularity.
ambiguities.evidence: kappa_2(R_k) is defined using R_k^(-1), condition (3) uses kappa_2(R_k), and the paragraph after the theorem says restriction (3) assures R is nonsingular. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: kappa_2 definition, condition (3), and following paragraph.)
ambiguities.impact: Without an unstated convention that a singular matrix has infinite condition number, the hypothesis already presupposes invertibility; the source does not resolve this logical presentation detail.

ambiguities.issue: The scope of the floating-point model beyond the displayed addition formula is not explicit in the selected passage.
ambiguities.evidence: The setup assumes IEEE arithmetic but displays only fl(x+y)=(x+y)(1+delta), |delta|<=epsilon_M, for normalized-range results, even though Algorithm 2 also uses products, dot products, division, norms, subtraction, and square roots. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and floating-point-model paragraph.)
ambiguities.impact: The contract must not silently strengthen the source to a fully specified rounding mode or detailed per-operation model.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem's inequalities suppress higher-order terms.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 1 says equations (4)-(8) hold 'to within terms of O(epsilon_M^2)', and the proof of (7) explicitly ends with +O(epsilon_M^2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: qualifier before equations (4)-(8); PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: norm estimate deriving (7).)
ambiguities.impact: Reading equation (7) as an exact inequality with no remainder for arbitrary epsilon_M would be stronger than the paper's stated first-order claim.

ambiguities.issue: A displayed square-root relation in the proof of (6) appears inconsistent with the first-order derivation.
ambiguities.evidence: The proof prints 1+c_3(m,k)epsilon_M+O(epsilon_M^2)=sqrt(1+c_2(m,k)), while the preceding inequality contains 1+c_2(m,k)epsilon_M and the theorem explicitly defines c_3=0.5c_2. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: derivation of equation (6); PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition of c_3.)
ambiguities.impact: This appears to omit epsilon_M inside the square root. The unambiguous theorem definition c_3=0.5c_2 and equation (6) should be preserved rather than literalizing the inconsistent proof display.

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 1 does not restate the dimensions and rank assumption.
ambiguities.evidence: The real m-by-n, m>=n, rank-n setup appears before Algorithms 1 and 2, whereas Theorem 1 begins directly with the floating-point and condition-number assumptions. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: standing setup; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: opening of Theorem 1.)
ambiguities.impact: These conditions are inherited standing context, not new explicit binders in the theorem paragraph itself.

contract_plain_english: Start with a real full-column-rank m-by-n matrix A, m >= n, and run the floating-point CGS-P algorithm whose diagonal is computed by the pythagorean/Cholesky-like formula, not by the standard residual norm. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: standing setup and distinction from CGS-S; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2.) For every leading prefix k, assume c_4(m,k)epsilon_M kappa_2(R_k)^2 < 1. Then, up to neglected O(epsilon_M^2) terms, the computed prefix has a small QR residual, a small normal-equation residual, nearly the same 2-norm as A_k, loss of orthogonality at most c_4(m,k)kappa_2(R_k)^2epsilon_M, and ||Q_k||_2 <= sqrt(2). (PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1, equations (3)-(8).) The orthogonality result follows by writing Q_k=(A_k+Delta A_k)R_k^(-1) and decomposing I-Q_k^TQ_k into the normal-equation error E_k, two linear factorization-error terms, and the quadratic Delta A_k term. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 312, anchor: exact identity and norm estimate deriving (7).)
